criterion: The tests that pinned the epoch integer are updated to pin the new form deliberately, not deleted
summary: Both original tests remain, in the stronger form the first review confirmed. Two further corrections it asked for are done. _timestamp's first try now catches OverflowError as well: SQLite round-trips 9e999 to inf, int(inf) raised out of sessions(), and the blanket handler in _codex_verdicts then dropped every Codex session rather than the one with the bad column - pinned by test_an_infinite_column_costs_one_session_and_not_every_session, which asserts the good row survives beside the bad one. And the unrenderable-column test reached only the ValueError arm, because the millisecond division runs first; each arm needs a different magnitude and SQLite's 64-bit INTEGER cannot hold enough to reach the other two, so the test now uses REAL columns with 1e18, 1e21 and 1e24, measured to raise ValueError, OSError and OverflowError respectively. Its guard narrows the tuple to one arm instead of emptying it, which subsumes the old mutation; the narrower test it replaced was removed as a strict subset rather than left as duplication. Guards: 6 of 6 pinned. Suites: 414 tests OK on 3.12.12 and 414 OK on 3.10.19; black and mypy clean over 37 files.
